slate.note: The official August 2026 Slate Levy is 61.38 c/l, down 52.56 c/l from 113.94 c/l. The live September headline remains anchored to the CEF daily accumulated over/(under)-recovery and is not manually adjusted again for the slate.

news.title: Official CEF 13 August snapshot points to September increases across all liquid fuels
news.source: Central Energy Fund (official daily BFP report)
news.credibility: Direct official CEF daily Basic Fuel Price report
news.summary: Average under-recoveries through 13 August imply Petrol 95 +R0.73871/l, Petrol 93 +R0.62883/l, Diesel 500ppm +R2.72505/l, Diesel 50ppm +R2.88609/l and illuminating paraffin +R2.14765/l for September if the review closed at that point.

news.title: August official adjustment: petrol down 52c, diesel and paraffin sharply higher
news.summary: Effective 5 August: both petrol grades -52c/l; diesel 500ppm +R1.3844/l; diesel 50ppm +R1.2344/l; wholesale illuminating paraffin +R1.52/l. The Slate Levy fell to 61.38c/l.

news.title: August LPG maximum: Zone 1A R33.44/kg; Saudi August CP rises for September benchmark
news.credibility: Official South African LPG maximum plus Reuters-sourced Saudi CP reporting
news.summary: The official Zone 1A residential LPG maximum is R33.44/kg for 5 August to 1 September. Saudi August CP rose to $620/t propane and $640/t butane, lifting the 60/40 benchmark to $628/t for the next model cycle.

news.title: Public reporting on the 16 July CEF snapshot showed a less severe diesel outlook
news.source: EWN / Stuff reporting on CEF data
news.credibility: Reputable reporting; superseded by the 17 July official CEF PDF
news.summary: The widely reported 16 July snapshot was Petrol 93 -R1.07/l, Petrol 95 -R1.03/l, Diesel 500ppm +R0.01/l and Diesel 50ppm -R0.24/l. The site now prioritises the newer official 17 July CEF report.

news.title: Saudi Aramco cuts July propane to $580/t and butane to $600/t
news.credibility: Reuters report based on trader pricing
news.summary: The 60/40 South African benchmark falls from about $784/t to $588/t. This is the main reason the August LPG model points to a large decrease.

news.title: South Africa confirms July LPG maximums and Saldanha special price
news.summary: The official July adjustment raised LPG by 16c/kg nationally and 19c/kg in the Western Cape. Saldanha MRP is R40.84/kg.

news.title: VLGC charter rates surge, limiting how much of the CP cut reaches retail
news.summary: A reported 90-day VLGC fixture near $280,000/day shows that freight is the biggest offsetting risk to the lower Saudi benchmark.

news.title: Africa LPG growth remains constrained by terminals, storage and rail
news.summary: Import-terminal and inland logistics constraints can keep regional delivered prices firmer than the international benchmark alone suggests.

news.title: South African LPG pricing uses Saudi CP rather than Petrol 93
news.summary: The old Petrol 93 proxy was replaced so the MRGP reflects the actual import cost of LPG.

news.title: Global LPG supply growth drove steep July benchmark cuts
news.summary: Saudi Arabia and Algeria both reduced July LPG selling prices as global supply improved, supporting a lower August South African import-parity input.

news.title: Mont Belvieu propane softened into July
news.summary: A softer US propane benchmark supports the broader view that international LPG supply conditions eased after the June spike.

news.title: Final August LPG price still depends on the review-period rand and landed costs
news.summary: The Saudi CP cut is known, but freight, insurance, storage, stock financing, exchange rate and regulatory rounding determine the final official decrease.

news.title: Brent settled at $89.22 as Middle East shipping risk stayed elevated
news.summary: Brent reached a one-month high. Continued Hormuz and Red Sea risk raises crude, freight and refined-product costs.

news.title: Refining bottlenecks are pushing fuel products faster than crude
news.summary: The crack spread matters directly to South Africa because the BFP uses finished petrol, diesel and kerosene benchmarks rather than Brent alone.

news.title: Latest published CEF-based outlook leaves petrol relief but diesel near or above flat
news.summary: The cited 16 July snapshot showed Petrol 93 down about R1.07, Petrol 95 down R1.03, Diesel 500ppm up about 1c and Diesel 50ppm down about 24c.

news.title: USD/ZAR traded near R16.50, close to the CEF reference level
news.summary: Foreign exchange is not the dominant current risk. Refined-product prices and shipping remain the larger drivers.

news.title: Government confirms July Slate Levy of 113.94c/l and full fuel levies
news.summary: The Slate Levy is part of petrol and diesel price structures but not the daily CEF BFP indicator. Any August change must be shown separately.

news.title: A durable ceasefire remains the largest downside-price catalyst
news.credibility: Scenario based on cited market reports
news.summary: A credible reopening of shipping routes could lower both crude and product premiums before the review closes.

news.title: Official BFP methodology uses refined-product import parity, not Brent alone
news.summary: Petrol uses Mediterranean and Singapore markers; diesel and paraffin use Mediterranean and Arabian Gulf products plus import costs.

lpg.summary: August Saudi Contract Prices rose by USD 40/t versus July. The 60/40 propane-butane benchmark rises from USD 588/t to USD 628/t, equal to about R0.65/kg at R16.1606/USD before freight, insurance, storage, financing, margins, VAT and official rounding. The September LPG retail figure remains a model; the final gazetted maximum overrides it.
lpg.methodNote: LPG is modelled separately from petrol and diesel. South Africa uses an import-parity LPG framework based on Saudi Contract Prices and import/logistics costs. Brent and CEF fuel recoveries are secondary context, not the direct LPG price marker.

fuel.benchmark: Mediterranean Premium Unleaded 95 FOB cargo + Singapore Mogas 95 FOB spot
fuel.note: Petrol 95 is the South African price-marker grade. The CEF recovery is the accessible official daily output of the proprietary spot basket.

fuel.benchmark: Petrol 95 marker less the Singapore 95/92 octane differential, prorated for 93 octane
fuel.note: The monthly adjustment follows the 95 marker; the 93-versus-95 differential is recalculated at the start of each quarter.

fuel.benchmark: Mediterranean gasoil sulphur interpolation + Arabian Gulf 0.05% gasoil FOB spot and premium
fuel.note: Tracks middle-distillate product prices, not Brent alone. Freight and product cracks can move diesel sharply.

fuel.benchmark: Mediterranean 1000ppm/10ppm interpolation + calculated Arabian Gulf 50ppm gasoil FOB and premium
fuel.note: The low-sulphur calculation uses sulphur differentials to derive the applicable 50ppm product value.

fuel.benchmark: Mediterranean Jet A1 FOB cargo + premium and Arabian Gulf Jet/Kero FOB spot + premium
fuel.note: The official method also includes a quality premium. Paraffin follows the kerosene/jet market and has no Slate Levy.

fuel.benchmark: USD/ZAR exchange rate at the official daily observation time
fuel.note: A weaker rand raises the landed rand cost even when dollar product prices are unchanged.

fuel.benchmark: Worldscale route freight adjusted through the applicable freight assessment methodology
fuel.note: Shipping risk and vessel availability affect the delivered import-parity value.

fuel.benchmark: Worldscale demurrage allowance
fuel.note: Compensates for vessel detention during loading and discharge.

fuel.benchmark: Insurance and associated import costs
fuel.note: Covers insurance, letters of credit, surveyors, agents and laboratory costs.

fuel.benchmark: Ocean loss allowance
fuel.note: Allowance for typical uninsurable product losses during marine transport.

fuel.benchmark: Cargo dues / wharfage tariff
fuel.note: Cost of using South African harbour facilities to discharge imported product.

fuel.benchmark: Coastal storage and handling
fuel.note: Recovers the regulated/deemed cost of coastal terminal storage and handling.

fuel.benchmark: Stock financing
fuel.market: Landed cost and South African prime rate
fuel.note: Finances the deemed stockholding period used in the import-parity calculation.

fuel.benchmark: Daily unit over/under recovery and cumulative Slate Account
fuel.note: The Slate Levy can alter petrol and diesel prices separately from the core BFP move.

fuel.benchmark: Magisterial District Zone transport differential
fuel.note: Road, rail and pipeline transport costs create different official prices by zone.

fuel.benchmark: Brent crude oil
fuel.note: Useful for direction and risk, but the BFP uses finished-product prices rather than Brent by itself.

fuel.benchmark: Gasoline crack spread and refinery availability
fuel.note: Explains why petrol may move differently from crude oil.

fuel.benchmark: Gasoil, diesel and jet/kerosene crack spreads
fuel.note: The most useful early-warning proxy for diesel and paraffin when proprietary spot assessments are unavailable.

fuel.benchmark: CEF daily Basic Fuel Price over/under-recovery table by grade
fuel.note: The most important accessible input for a South African monthly forecast. It captures the official product basket, exchange rate and landed-cost methodology up to the publication date.

fuel.benchmark: Monthly DMPR price adjustment and gazetted price schedules
fuel.note: The final announced result supersedes every model and is used for accuracy scoring and price-board updates.

fuel.benchmark: General Fuel Levy
fuel.note: A policy-controlled component that can change pump prices independently of international product markets.

fuel.benchmark: Road Accident Fund Levy
fuel.note: Applies to petrol and diesel and is separate from the BFP movement.

fuel.benchmark: Customs and Excise Levy
fuel.note: A regulated domestic impost included after the international BFP component.

fuel.benchmark: Regulated wholesale and retail margins
fuel.note: Petrol retail is regulated; changes in allowable margins can move the pump price even when BFP is unchanged.

fuel.benchmark: Published wholesale margin and retail guidance
fuel.note: Diesel retail prices are not nationally fixed, so the published wholesale benchmark and local dealer margin must be kept separate.

fuel.benchmark: Demand Side Management Levy on 95 unleaded petrol
fuel.note: A product-specific domestic component that should not be applied to diesel, paraffin or LPG.

fuel.benchmark: Tracer Dye Levy
fuel.note: Supports control of unlawful mixing and misuse of marked products.

fuel.benchmark: Petroleum Pipelines Levy
fuel.note: Supports pipeline regulation and forms part of the domestic build-up rather than the international BFP.

fuel.benchmark: Dubai/Oman sour crude marker
fuel.current: Monitor direction and spread to Brent
fuel.note: Useful context for Arabian Gulf refiners and middle-distillate economics, but not a substitute for the finished-product basket.

fuel.benchmark: Clean-product tanker rates and marine bunker fuel
fuel.note: Tanker tightness and bunker costs help anticipate freight pressure before the official landed-cost outcome is fully visible.

fuel.benchmark: Mediterranean and Singapore gasoline cracks, inventories and refinery outages
fuel.note: Adds early warning for the remaining review period and helps distinguish petrol from crude-oil moves.

fuel.benchmark: Gasoil and jet/kerosene inventories, cracks and refinery outages
fuel.note: The strongest explanatory proxy when diesel and paraffin diverge from petrol.

fuel.benchmark: OPEC+ supply policy and geopolitical disruption score
fuel.note: Used to widen best/worst ranges, not to replace the official product-price calculation.

fuel.benchmark: US and OECD petroleum inventory trends
fuel.current: Monitor gasoline and distillate stocks separately
fuel.note: Inventory direction helps confirm whether product-market pressure is persistent or temporary.

lpg.benchmark: Saudi Aramco propane Contract Price / official selling price
lpg.note: South Africa uses the monthly Saudi Contract Price as the core import-parity product benchmark.

lpg.benchmark: Saudi Aramco butane Contract Price / official selling price
lpg.note: Combined with propane using the South African 60/40 blend assumption.

lpg.benchmark: Weighted Saudi CP blend
lpg.note: July weighted CP was $588/t; August is $628/t before landed costs and local regulated price components.

lpg.benchmark: USD/ZAR exchange rate
lpg.note: Converts the dollar CP and import costs into rand per kilogram.

lpg.benchmark: Time Charter Equivalent freight for a suitable LPG carrier / VLGC
lpg.market: Middle East to South African ports
lpg.note: The largest uncertainty in the current forecast; high charter rates can absorb part of the CP decrease.

lpg.benchmark: Insurance and associated import costs
lpg.note: Official regulation specifies 0.15% of free-on-board value plus freight.

lpg.benchmark: Storage and handling at coastal terminals
lpg.note: Based on the cost of coastal LPG storage and handling facilities.

lpg.benchmark: Demurrage rate
lpg.note: Compensation payable for vessel detention beyond the contracted loading or discharge time.

lpg.benchmark: Cargo dues
lpg.note: Harbour facility cost for offloading LPG at South African ports.

lpg.benchmark: Stock financing
lpg.market: Landed LPG cost and South African prime rate
lpg.note: Financing cost based on landed values, allowed stockholding days and prime less two percentage points.

lpg.benchmark: Maximum Refinery Gate Price (MRGP)
lpg.note: The regulated maximum at which a refinery or importer may market LPG.

lpg.benchmark: Maximum Retail Price by pricing zone
lpg.note: The dashboard tracks coastal Zone 1A, inland Zone 9C and the separate Saldanha maximum.

lpg.benchmark: Sonatrach propane and butane OSP
lpg.note: Useful confirmation of global LPG direction, but not the South African formula marker.

lpg.benchmark: Argus Far East Index / Asia delivered LPG assessments
lpg.note: Shows Asian delivered demand and freight pressure around the Saudi CP reference.

lpg.benchmark: Mont Belvieu propane/butane and US inventories
lpg.note: A useful global supply signal, but not a direct input to the South African regulated formula.

lpg.benchmark: VLGC spot rates, Panama/Hormuz/Red Sea route risk and bunker fuel
lpg.note: Used to widen the best-to-worst forecast range when official landed freight is not yet known.

lpg.benchmark: Primary transport differential by LPG pricing zone
lpg.current: Reflected in Zone 1A and Zone 9C maximums
lpg.note: Explains why inland LPG maximums differ from coastal maximums even when the same MRGP is used.

lpg.benchmark: Operating-expense allowance
lpg.market: DMPR LPG maximum retail price structure
lpg.note: Adjusted under the regulated retail framework and separate from Saudi CP and ocean freight.

lpg.benchmark: Working-capital allowance in the retail price structure
lpg.market: DMPR LPG maximum retail price structure
lpg.note: Covers financing needs in the local retail/distribution chain and is distinct from import stock financing.

lpg.benchmark: Depreciation allowance
lpg.market: DMPR LPG maximum retail price structure
lpg.note: A regulated local component adjusted separately from the monthly import benchmark.

lpg.benchmark: Gross margin allowance
lpg.market: DMPR LPG maximum retail price structure
lpg.note: Part of the regulated maximum retail build-up after the MRGP and transport components.

lpg.benchmark: VAT and official rounding
lpg.note: Applied in the final maximum retail price and can create small differences from a raw benchmark-only estimate.

lpg.benchmark: Saldanha Bay special MRGP and MRP route
lpg.market: Port of Saldanha Bay / Western Cape
lpg.note: Must be tracked separately from the normal coastal Zone 1A maximum because the special import route has its own gazetted values.

lpg.benchmark: US EIA propane/propylene inventories and exports
lpg.note: Useful for confirming global LPG supply tightness, but not a direct South African pricing input.

lpg.benchmark: Saudi CP versus Argus Far East Index / FEI spread
lpg.note: Helps explain whether Saudi CP is likely to remain firm or soften and whether delivered Asian demand is absorbing supply.

lpg.benchmark: VLGC fleet utilisation, newbuilding deliveries and route availability
lpg.note: Distinguishes a temporary freight spike from a persistent vessel-supply shortage.

lpg.benchmark: Local refinery, import terminal, rail and storage availability
lpg.note: Can affect availability and delivery economics even when the official maximum retail price falls.

lpg.benchmark: South African winter demand and load-shedding substitution
lpg.note: Used for stock and delivery timing, not as a direct input to the regulated maximum price.

lpg.benchmark: Cylinder filling, distribution capacity and delivered-cost spread
lpg.note: Supports store decisions because the gazetted maximum and the actual delivered purchase cost are not the same thing.

forecastGovernance.liquidFuelAnchor: Latest available official CEF daily over/under-recovery by grade; reputable predictor pages are secondary live fallbacks only.
forecastGovernance.liquidFuelEngine: CEF anchor + remaining-review-period finished-product, FX and landed-cost scenarios + policy layer
forecastGovernance.lpgAnchor: 60% Saudi propane CP + 40% Saudi butane CP
forecastGovernance.lpgEngine: Weighted Saudi CP + USD/ZAR + LPG freight/insurance/storage/demurrage/port/finance + regulated retail components
forecastGovernance.separationRule: LPG never uses the petrol/diesel CEF recovery or Slate Levy. Brent is context, not the direct marker for either engine.
forecastGovernance.confidenceRule: Confidence falls when the official anchor is stale, the review period is incomplete, product/freight volatility is high, or direct benchmark coverage is incomplete.
forecastGovernance.publicationRule: Prefer the newest dated official CEF report, retain source/date health, and never overwrite a newer official anchor with an older secondary snapshot.
